rules.disposition: Per identity (R021-C/1 §8): reject if a registered gate fails (correctness, determinism, accounting, identity/P1, certificate validity, unsupported-scope rule) or a pre-registered hypothesis is refuted; inconclusive if every gate passes but a primary question cannot be evaluated (zero eligible cells, missing/incomplete records, coverage); keep_experimental otherwise. A functional implementation needs no win; no adoption, no loss tolerance.
rules.host_sleep: Registered after stage T (whose host slept; its timings are contaminated, statuses valid) and before any L/R/M/I execution, never as a post-hoc filter: those stages run under a `caffeinate -i -m -s -w <executor pid>` assertion started by the executor; the executor captures `pmset -g log` sleep/wake transitions for the stage window (`pmset-sleep-wake.txt`) beside the load samples; a timing window with any `Sleep` transition is `slept`, one over the load threshold `contaminated`, one without load samples or without the registered sleep log `unknown` -- all three are inconclusive timing. Monotonic solve clocks and hard-wall deadlines exclude sleep; statuses are unaffected.
rules.infrastructure_deviation: An invocation whose process ends without a complete manifest because of infrastructure (host restart, OOM kill, disk full, tool/auth failure; evidence recorded) may be re-executed ONCE into a fresh slot `<id>.retry1`; the failed attempt stays in the ledger and is reported as a deviation. A completed run is never re-executed, whatever its statuses or timings; solver timeouts/failures are outcomes, never retry reasons; host load is never a retry reason.
rules.nominee: For each `kind: nominee` comparison, over every scheduled (case, algorithm) of its algorithms on its tuning bundles: failures(v) = cells with status timeout, invalid_plan, algorithm_error, model_error, incomplete_snapshot, cancelled or missing; shortfall(v) = cells ok at some scanned value but at v not ok, or ok with gross below that cell's best gross over all scanned values. Nominee = the smallest v with shortfall(v) = 0 and failures(v) = min over the scan; if none qualifies, the canonical value 4. No loss tolerance, no timing criterion; `apply: false` results are informational only. Registered before any tuning observation (tools/research_021/analysis.py `nominee`).
rules.numerical_tolerances: None added. Protocol math and evaluation are exact integers. cfmm_dual's residual tolerance is its pinned preset value (a numerical residual criterion, never a bound); float ratios (recovered/estimate, geometric means) are reported, never thresholded.
rules.statuses: Every scheduled cell keeps its status (ok, no_route, unsupported, timeout, invalid_plan, incomplete_snapshot, model_error, algorithm_error, cancelled, missing); unconditional counts use the full schedule. Paired quality uses common-OK cells only; a missing score is N/A, never 0; a zero baseline gross is N/A, counted apart.
rules.stops_fallback_failure: As each identity's research contract (history-labels.md §7, integer-allocation.md §5.4-5.6, suffix-repair.md §5.7, cycle-safe-sor.md §4.5-4.7, cfmm-dual.md §5.4, §6-6.1). A fallback plan is labelled from the record (`search_stats.r021.fallback`, `search.cfmm.fallback`), never counted as the mechanism's result; a budget-bound cell proves no identity.
rules.ties: Exact integer gross comparison: equal gross is a tie (neither higher nor lower); no money tolerance. Solver-internal tie rules are each identity's research contract's.
rules.timing: L01 labels (latency-baseline.md §4). A batch window whose sampled 1-minute load exceeds 0.5 x logical CPUs, or has no sample, is `inconclusive`; one sample per case gives no A/A noise floor, so batch timing is descriptive only. Speed verdicts exist only in stage L via `report.latency compare` (L01 rules verbatim). No single-request percentile, no SLA, no total-campaign runtime ceiling.
